mustFail: a line never runs through another mark's point: a big sell under a small one on the same candle keeps only its point, since a sell's card never goes below
two sells on one candle: the bigger keeps its card above, the other keeps only its point rather than run its line through the bigger one's point or flip below
two sells pinned under the top edge: the newer takes the short room above, the older has no clean room on its side and keeps only its point, never a card below
a card stays in the pane: the line shortens near an edge, the card slides in from the sides, a side with no room leaves only the point, and a crowded card slides sideways on its side
a live iceberg inside a bigger mark on its candle still gets its card first, its line starting at the bigger mark's edge, and the bigger one, with its own side taken, keeps only its point
a mark that only partly overlaps another keeps its line on its own mark, and two buys sharing the one side below leave the second with only its point
a sell's card is above and a buy's below, whatever is nearer: a sell under a tall wick runs its line up past the wick, and a candle that walls its side leaves only the point
a buy iceberg's line runs straight down from the point of contact to a card below it, a sell's straight up to a card above
a card keeps last frame's slot while it is still clean and on its side, and gives it up when it is not
placed on the candle, a sell's mark sits at the candle's high and a buy's at its low, the card still on its side; a candle with no bar under it keeps the price
